thread:
Asha: Hey @devex — running into weird behavior in the Go sampleapp generator. If the client cancels a context and immediately retries, sometimes we get duplicated partial responses (same tokens repeated) and our runtime KV cache shows duplicate entries. Anyone seen this? Repro below.

Marco: Hmm can you paste the minimal snippet you used?

Asha: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resCh := make(chan string)
go func() {
  gresp, _ := client.Generate(ctx, req)
  for tok := range gresp.Stream() { resCh <- tok }
  close(resCh)
}()
for t := range resCh { fmt.Print(t) }
```

Sam: my guess: reusing the same Generator instance across retries. If the goroutine is canceled mid-handshake, internal stream/handshake state isn't fully reset and buffered bytes can get replayed on reconnect.

Tracy: Seen this too. Often hits when auth-refresh (401 -> refresh -> reconnect) happens mid-stream. Pre-handshake bytes get buffered by transport and replayed.

Asha: Repro steps: call Generate, cancel after ~150ms, immediately call Generate again with the same Generator. Repro rate ~30% on my laptop.

DevExBot: Filed issue #4823 — gen:stream:duplicate-on-retry

Marco: Quick workaround: construct a new Generator per retry or explicitly drain/flush the previous stream before returning. Approx pattern:
```go
// safe retry pattern (illustrative)
func safeGenerate(ctx context.Context, g *sdk.Generator, req Req) (string, error) {
  ctx2, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  it, err := g.Generate(ctx2, req)
  if err != nil { return "", err }
  // drain to avoid leftover buffered bytes on transport
  for {
    _, ok := it.Next()
    if !ok { break }
  }
  return it.Result(), nil
}
```

Sam: we should add a sample showing tradeoffs: generator-per-retry vs reused-generator and the latency/cost implications. Also show the explicit drain pattern.

Tracy: and docs should call out auth-refresh gotchas: recommend integrating token rotation at transport layer (so handshake isn't interrupted mid-stream) rather than reauthing at request time.

Asha: I'll add a tiny sampleapp and an onboarding doc section. Plan: small reproducible test, sample showing safe pattern, and an e2e that aggressively cancels mid-handshake.

Marco: I have a small harness from runtime fuzzing that can spam cancel/retry locally, ping me and I'll share it.

Asha: pinging @Sam for review once the PR is up :eyes:

Sam: happy to review. :+1:
